# Local Pug inputs

All 36 pinned upstream blobs remain unchanged under `upstream/`, including the original Rust 0.17 binding, build manifests and lockfile. The operational crate uses the retained ABI-14 generated parser with Tree-sitter LanguageFn 0.1.7 and cc 1.2.67. No build-time generation, acquisition or upstream build script runs. The upstream Cargo version is 0.0.1 and npm version is 1.0.0; the root wrapper version follows Cargo. The MIT grant is retained exactly, alongside the original npm ISC metadata discrepancy.

The separate active scanner uses a complete versioned 16-bit indentation wire capped at 1024 bytes, canonical atomic deserialization, checked state/allocation, finite accepted external-scanner logical steps and sticky typed refusal outside parser rollback. Speculative unmatched dedentation declines without changing state or claiming a token; parser recovery remains real syntax evidence. Embedded NUL, malformed state and lifecycle failures remain strict.

The thread-affine safe Rust guard retains a real C-held Rc count and a temporary Rc lease around every arbitrary cancellation probe. Probe storage is reserved fallibly in a one-element Vec; the constant-size Rc allocation is infallible on stable Rust. Callback and final-owner destruction panics do not unwind across C. Matching finish detaches before releasing the native count; reentry fails closed and forgetting retains valid owned storage. Memory enforcement remains unavailable.

The wrapper's contract string binds the actual generated parser, active scanner/status/header and the wrapper body with only that constant line omitted. The standalone-qualified wrapper body is unchanged. Native syntax recovery does not establish evaluated template output, JavaScript binding, imports, implicit elements, or runtime calls. Only intrinsic work/capacity refusal can support a complete source-preservation certificate; explicit caller limits and strict refusals do not grant partial syntax.
